To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a BCI based on CNN can be profitfully applied to decode SSVEP features for control of navigation in virtual environments.

1) the proposed approach is capable of controlling the navigation of the participant in the virtual environment; 2) the CNN based approach outperformed the traditional SSVEP classification approach based on linear discriminant analysis (LDA); 3) the CNN based classification approach was more robust to the presence of artifacts in the EEG signal.

a BCI based on CNN is capable of discriminating SSVEP features for the control of navigation in a virtual environment, thus enabling the control of the movement of a virtual avatar by the only brain activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a BCI based on SSVEP and a CNN, which is able to control navigation in a VE.
developing a non-invasive, wearable and low cost system for navigation in virtual environments, based on the SSVEP paradigm and a Convolutional neural network.
the design and development of a BCI based on SSVEP for navigation in a VE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BCI-SSVPE based navigation approach is a promising tool for the control of navigation in virtual environments.
the BCI-SSVP based navigation approach is a promising solution for navigation in virtual environments, which can be applied to assist the disabled in the daily life.
the CNN based BCI is a reliable and robust method to decode brain activity, thus allowing to navigate in the virtual environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed approach can be used as an alternative to traditional navigation interfaces, in order to provide the user with an enhanced experience of immersion, by means of a BCI based on CNN, which is able to decode the SSVEP features from EEG data in real time.
the CNN-based BCI can provide a reliable navigation control interface, which can be applied in the context of virtual rehabilitation.
a CNN-based BCI can be used for navigation in VE, where only a reduced number of classes are to be discriminated, and where the BCI is required to provide a fast response.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed approach could be used for the development of a BCI based navigation system for the control of a robotic wheelchair or a powered exoskeleton, thus enabling the control of a mobile robot by only using the brain activity.

the BCI-SSVP based navigation control can be successfully applied to control walking in VE, thus opening the way to a new generation of BCI-based applications for navigation in virtual and real environments.
a CNN-based BCI can be successfully applied in a real-time navigation task in VE, and can be a valid approach for the development of a BCI-SSVPE-based navigation system.
